Mandatory tiny-frame check: although DefaultBufferPool minimum tier is256 bytes, readDataFrame bypasses pooling entirely for frame payload<=1024, using exact make plus SliceBuffer; claiming every1-byte DATA allocates a256-byte pool buffer would be wrong. Compactor threshold counts recvMsg+slice header+payload and compacts the approximately1024-message small suffix. Above threshold, actual tiers include1025->4096 and4097->16384; checked these alongside queue capacity, copy/suffix storage, raw BufferSlice retention and aggregate E(R), rather than assuming raw wire length equals backing capacity. Stream.read retains fragments without mandatory materialization; consumed bytes retire flow-control delta, so raw fragments and queued DATA must be considered jointly, not as two independent maximum message allowances. Static windows retain maybeAdjust and independent connection replenishment as the proposal says. Close waits for writer completion or its bounded timeout, then reader/keepalive cleanup and stream close before ConnEnd: the proposal also requires raw-socket close, completed call unwind and buffer release, not context cancellation alone. Unknown cleanup keeps credit. No unconditional general writer-join guarantee was inferred from ConnEnd.
